analysis.title: How the bearish risks can offset each other
key_insights: November has been volatile: the average S&P 500 daily move this month is 1.2%, the most since April 2025 (Liberation Day tariffs). The 2yr Treasury yield rose 33bps last week, the biggest weekly jump since October 2024.
Three stress points have eased in recent weeks: oil (US-Iran escalation fears fell after the midterms), AI-related growth fears, and European fiscal stress.
Brent (current active January contract) fell from $113.43/bbl at end-October to $96.58/bbl, and near-term inflation swaps fell on both sides of the Atlantic.
The Philly semiconductor index rose over 12% from its November 5 lows to last Friday's close, and IG and HY credit spreads tightened on both sides of the Atlantic.
The Franco-German 10yr spread fell from a peak of 174bps on October 22 to 156bps, and long-end sovereign yields are below last month's highs.
The S&P 500 posted its first weekly gain after four consecutive declines. The 10yr Treasury yield had its biggest weekly jump since April 2025.

DB argues the three main bearish risks (Middle East oil and inflation, an AI growth slowdown hitting tech and equities, and European fiscal stress widening sovereign spreads) are often presented as one combined risk-off driver but are hard to see occurring together.

Mechanism: if AI growth fears rise, lower capex and productivity expectations and weaker equities push government bond yields down, which eases fiscal concerns. Demand-side inflation pressure (energy, memory chips) would also fall, making rate hikes less likely and easing front-end yields. An equity decline would also tighten financial conditions and lower the chance of hikes.

Last week markets priced in more rate hikes across the big central banks, unwinding the dovish repricing that followed the recent financial stress. DB likens this to the 2022-23 hiking cycle, when dovish repricings were repeatedly undone.

Causes of the hawkish repricing: an upside US CPI surprise (3m annualised core CPI for October +3.75%, the fastest since April 2024), no US-Iran deal (Trump said 'We don't need a deal with Iran'), and easier financial conditions from the tech recovery and tighter credit spreads.

Markets price 113bps of Fed hikes by the September 2027 meeting (25bps already delivered plus 88bps ahead). The day before the last hiking cycle began, markets priced only 95bps by the same horizon, so pricing has already passed that.

DB says investors tend to underestimate the scale of hiking cycles at the start and over-weight the odds of a dovish pivot after financial stress. A pivot is hard while headline and core inflation are above target, as in 2023 around SVB, when the Fed and ECB kept hiking.
The mechanism also runs the other way: if equities recover and spreads tighten, easier financial conditions let central banks prioritise inflation, so the chance of hikes rises again.

risk_factors: Oil: Middle East escalation would push oil and inflation higher.
AI growth slowdown: could trigger a tech selloff that spreads to equities more broadly.
European fiscal stress: could widen sovereign bond spreads.
Hawkish central banks: easier financial conditions from recovering equities and tighter spreads give central banks room to focus on inflation, raising the chance of rate hikes.
Markets have historically underestimated the scale of hiking cycles at the outset, and inflation above target makes a dovish pivot unlikely.

tension_points.theme: AI growth fears and rate hikes
tension_points.bull_case: Easing AI growth fears, tighter credit spreads and lower oil support equities and ease financial stress.
tension_points.bear_case: Easier financial conditions let central banks prioritise inflation, so rate hikes get priced back in, as in the past week. Markets historically underestimate the scale of hiking cycles at the outset.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A serious wobble in AI-related growth would dampen inflation and lower yields, reducing the chance of rate hikes.

theme_stances.key_argument: It would be very hard for the oil, AI growth and fiscal stress risks to occur simultaneously because they have offsetting influences.
theme_stances.evidence: it's difficult for all the current risk factors to occur simultaneously

theme_stances.key_argument: Markets tend to underestimate the scale of hiking cycles at the start, and a dovish pivot is hard with inflation above target.
theme_stances.evidence: markets have consistently tended to underestimate the scale of rate hiking cycles at the start
